title: observability: token/KV cost & latency logging, dashboard updates, and alert tuning
author: Priya Patel
release_notes: Adds token-level KV cache cost/latency logging, new Grafana dashboard panels for token/KV breakdowns, and tuned alert thresholds for high miss-rate and high-latency cache paths.
description:
Motivation: We need better visibility into per-token KV cache cost and latency to attribute inference unit economics to prompt patterns and to catch regression in cache performance. This PR adds structured token/KV metrics and logging, dashboard panels to visualize token-level cost/latency breakdowns, and alert tuning for cache miss spikes and high tail latencies.

What this change does: - Emits token_kv_* metrics from the runtime emitter (hits, misses, miss_cost_us, latency_ms percentiles) with controlled cardinality. - Adds a parsing pipeline to ingest and transform token-level logs into Prometheus/Grafana-friendly metrics and traces. - Adds Grafana dashboard JSON with new token/KV panels and example queries for cost-per-token, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and KV miss-rate. - Adds alert rules (Prometheus alertmanager) tuned to sample-based thresholds and integrates runbook links. - Updates docs and runbook with query examples, thresholds, and rollback steps.

Checklist: - [x] Emit metrics and logs from runtime - [x] Parse/ingest pipeline & unit tests - [x] New dashboard panels + templating variables - [x] Alert rules added and thresholds tuned with SRE - [x] Docs and runbook updated - [x] Staging validation with replayed traces

Testing performed: Unit tests for token_kv_parser and runtime emitter. Integration tests in staging with synthetic workload that reproduces high-miss and normal-miss scenarios. Dashboard validated against replayed traces from last 7 days. CI flake fixed and re-run.

Rollout: Gradual rollout (see rollout_plan field) with an opt-out env var to disable token-level logging if we see unexpected cardinality or performance regressions.

Notes: We intentionally limit per-token labeling and instead emit aggregated buckets and sampled example payloads in order to keep cardinality bounded. SRE reviewed alert thresholds; we tuned p95 latency alert to 120ms for cache layer and miss-rate alert to 1.5% per-minute for high-traffic routes. Related Linear: ENG-3421, ENG-3498. Support ticket SUP-8812 requested better bill-of-cost visibility for a customer-facing incident earlier this quarter.

review_comments: Evan Li: Can we avoid adding high-cardinality labels per token? Prometheus cardinality is a concern for long-running clusters.
Priya Patel: We addressed this by emitting aggregated buckets (per-route/model buckets) and restricted sampled example payloads. Added config to cap unique tag values and added sampling rate control.
Marco Ruiz: The p95 threshold of 120ms seems aggressive for some models. Can SRE confirm expected tail latency?
Samantha Green: SRE reviewed with Marco — we tuned p95 to 120ms for cache layer only and added a suppression window during rollout. Updated alert message to include affected route and recent delta.
Evan Li: Please add an opt-out environment flag to disable token-level logs if we see unexpected effects.
Priya Patel: Opt-out flag added (pkg/config/feature_flags.go) and documented in runbook.
testing_notes: Unit tests: tests/observability/test_kv_logging.py ran locally and in CI
Staging: replayed synthetic traces for 7 days worth of traffic to validate dashboards and alerts
Load: validated emitter CPU impact under 2% in staging with sampling enabled
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Merge to main and enable token-KV logging in staging for 48h
Stage 1: Canary 10% of prod traffic for 48h; monitor token_kv_miss_rate and token_kv_latency_p95
Stage 2: Increase to 50% for 72h if metrics stable
Stage 3: Full rollout and remove suppression window after 7 days
Rollback: Disable token-level logging via FEATURE_TOKEN_KV_LOGGING=false and revert alerts if cardinality/cost regressions observed
additional_context: Related to ENG-3421 (token-level cost attribution) and ENG-3498 (cache performance regressions)
Customer support ticket SUP-8812 requested per-route cost breakdown which motivated this work
Cardinality guards and sampling were reviewed with SRE to avoid long-term Prometheus explosion
